key_insight: MedJev delivers competitive zero-shot medical predictions in a single forward pass, but patient-level confidence estimates require local recalibration.
clinical_relevance: Laptop-based inference could support low-compute clinical decision research, though benchmark performance does not establish safety or benefit in clinical practice.
method: Evaluated an open System One model across 10 medical benchmarks without generating text.
Compared zero-shot predictions with LLM baselines, published GPT results, and supervised models.
Tested two-parameter local recalibration using 50–200 labeled examples.
evidence_signal: MedJev achieved 72.5% MedQA accuracy and 0.926 in-hospital mortality AUROC on MIMIC-based evaluation; reported recalibration reduced mortality expected calibration error from 0.286 to 0.007.
watch_item: Performance varied by task: ED admission AUROC lagged a supervised comparator (0.745 vs. 0.809), and strong discrimination did not ensure reliable confidence estimates.
paper_title: MedJev: Evaluating Zero-Shot System-One Decision Making in Medicine
